title_en: Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Group Corporation v. Harbin Fucheng Catering Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch — dispute over infringement of registered trademark exclusive right and unfair competition
ruling_gist_en: 1. Pursuant to Article 1(1) of the Judicial Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Application of Law in Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks, where a party prominently uses characters identical or similar to another party's registered trademark as its enterprise name on the same or similar goods, likely to cause confusion among relevant public, such act constitutes harm to the exclusive right to use the registered trademark. Pursuant to Article 7(2) of the Opinions of the State Trademark Office on Several Issues Concerning Protection of Service Marks, the normal use of customary marks in the service industry, and the normal use of trade names (shop names), personal names, place names, or names of service premises to indicate service characteristics or to explain service matters, does not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a service mark, unless there is a manifest intention of unfair competition. According to the above provisions, when an enterprise uses characters identical or similar to another party's registered trademark as its trade name on the same or similar goods, it shall follow the principle of good faith. Where an actor, with the purpose of riding on the fame of another's well-known trademark and confusing the relevant public's perception of the relevant goods, arbitrarily abbreviates its own trade name and uses it on goods, such act constitutes infringement of another party's exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

full_text_en:
Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Group Corporation v. Harbin Fucheng Food Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch — dispute over infringement of registered trademark rights and unfair competition

Ruling Summary

I. Pursuant to Article 1(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademark Disputes, the use of characters identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the enterprise name in a prominent manner on identical or similar goods, where such use is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public, constitutes an act of infringement upon the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. According to Paragraph 2 of Article 7 of the State Trademark Office's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Protection of Service Marks, the normal use by others of customary signs in the service industry, as well as the normal use of trade names (enterprise names), personal names, place names, and names of service premises to indicate the characteristics of the service or to explain matters relating to the service, shall not constitute an act of infringement upon the exclusive right to use a service mark, except where there is a clear intention of unfair competition. Pursuant to the above provisions, when an enterprise uses characters identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as its enterprise name on identical or similar goods, it shall abide by the principle of good faith. Where a party, for the purpose of free-riding on a well-known trademark of another person and confusing the relevant public's perception of the relevant goods, arbitrarily simplifies its own enterprise name for use on goods, such act constitutes an act of infringement upon the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of another person.

II. Article 5 of the Law Against Unfair Competition provides: "Business operators shall not engage in the following unfair means in market transactions to harm competitors: (1) counterfeiting another person's registered trademark; (2) without authorization, using the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known product of another person, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to that of another person's well-known product, thereby causing confusion with the well-known product of another person and leading purchasers to mistake it for that well-known product; ..." Pursuant to the above provision, the act of, without authorization, using the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known product of another person, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to that of another person's well-known product, thereby causing confusion with the well-known product of another person and leading consumers to mistake it for that well-known product, constitutes an act of unfair competition.

Plaintiff: Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Group Corporation, domiciled at: Xinglongzhuang, Sanhe City, Hebei Province.
Legal Representative: Li Gaoqi, Chairman of the Board.
Defendant: Harbin Fucheng Food Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch, domiciled at: Fork Street, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.
Responsible Person: Chen Mengdi, Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Sanhe Fucheng Company), initiated a lawsuit before the Kunming Intermediate People's Court of Yunnan Province against the defendant, Harbin Fucheng Food Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch (hereinafter referred to as Kunming Fucheng Company), for infringement of registered trademark rights and unfair competition.

The plaintiff, Sanhe Fucheng Company, alleged: Sanhe Fucheng Company obtained a trademark registration certificate No. 1344801 from the State Trademark Office in 1999, granting it the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "福成" (Fucheng) for services such as restaurants and hotels. The defendant, Kunming Fucheng Company, without permission from the plaintiff, prominently used the registered trademark characters "福成" (Fucheng) in advertising text on the front, left side, and top of the door of its business premises, on in-store ordering cards, in advertising materials posted inside the store, and in leaflets distributed, and also, without authorization, used the name and unique decoration of the plaintiff's well-known service "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot), which was sufficient to cause confusion and misidentification among the relevant public, thereby infringing upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use a registered trademark and constituting unfair competition. The plaintiff requested the court to order Kunming Fucheng Company to cease using the enterprise name containing the characters "福成" (Fucheng), immediately cease all forms of advertising using the characters "福成" (Fucheng), replace promotional signs containing the characters "福成" (Fucheng), eliminate the adverse effects, publish an apology to Sanhe Fucheng Company in the *Kunming Daily*, and compensate Sanhe Fucheng Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 200,000.

The defendant, Kunming Fucheng Company, argued: 1. The registered trademark No. 1344801 involved in this case had already been transferred by the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company to a third party, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd., on April 7, 2003, and that company has since been dissolved. Therefore, Sanhe Fucheng Company lacks proper standing as a litigation party and has no right to bring this lawsuit. 2. The actions of Kunming Fucheng Company would not cause confusion or misidentification among the relevant public. "福成" (Fucheng), as the enterprise name of Kunming Fucheng Company, had been approved and registered by the administrative authority for industry and commerce as early as December 1997. The company is fully entitled to use its own enterprise name lawfully, which does not infringe upon the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of another person, nor does it constitute unfair competition. The defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

The following facts were found at first instance by the Kunming Intermediate People's Court:

The plaintiff, Sanhe Fucheng Company, is an enterprise primarily engaged in animal husbandry and related service operations. On December 14, 1999, Sanhe Fucheng Company obtained the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801. This trademark is a composite mark consisting of Chinese characters, pinyin, and a graphic (the upper part is the Chinese characters "福成"; the lower part is the pinyin "fucheng" accompanied by an ox-head pattern). The designated services for this trademark are restaurants, hotels, and animal breeding. Sanhe Fucheng Company began operating a hotpot catering business primarily featuring fat beef and engaged in franchise operations, using this registered trademark on the signboards and door headers of these business premises, and displaying alongside the trademark texts such as "福成肥牛" (Fucheng Fat Beef), "福成" (Fucheng), "福成肥牛城" (Fucheng Fat Beef City), and "福成肥牛海鲜城" (Fucheng Fat Beef Seafood City). On May 21, 2003, Sanhe Fucheng Company transferred this registered trademark to a third party, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd. On August 18, 2004, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd. entered into a trademark license contract with Sanhe Fucheng Company, stipulating that Sanhe Fucheng Company would obtain the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801 and the right to independently initiate litigation for rights protection. On the same day, the two parties also executed a power of attorney reiterating the above rights obtained by Sanhe Fucheng Company.

The defendant, Kunming Fucheng Company, is a branch of Harbin Fucheng Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Harbin Fucheng Company). Harbin Fucheng Company was registered and established on June 10, 1999, with a business scope covering catering and retail of tobacco and alcohol. It also operates a hotpot catering business primarily featuring fat beef and has also begun franchise operations. Kunming Fucheng Company displayed the text "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot) on the signboard hung outside its business premises, the text "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot) on the exterior wall of the store, and texts such as "福成肥牛火锅昆明旗舰店" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot Kunming Flagship Store) and the enterprise introduction of Harbin Fucheng Company in its promotional materials and ordering cards.

The disputed issues at first instance were: 1. Whether the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company had proper standing; 2. Whether the actions of the defendant Kunming Fucheng Company constituted proper use of its enterprise name within reasonable limits, or constituted infringement upon the registered trademark rights of another person.

The Kunming Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

I. Regarding the issue of whether the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company had proper standing. Article 53 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law) provides: "Where any of the acts infringing the exclusive right to use a registered trademark as listed in Article 52 of this Law occurs, the parties may settle the dispute through negotiation; if the parties are unwilling to negotiate or fail to reach an agreement through negotiation, the trademark registrant or an interested party may file a lawsuit with the People's Court, or may request the administrative authority for industry and commerce to handle the matter. ..." Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademark Disputes provides: "The term 'interested party' as used in Article 53 of the Trademark Law includes the licensee under a trademark license contract, the lawful heir to the property rights in a registered trademark, etc. Where the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is infringed, the licensee under an exclusive license contract may file a lawsuit with the People's Court; the licensee under a sole license contract may file a lawsuit jointly with the trademark registrant, or may file a lawsuit on its own if the trademark registrant fails to do so; the licensee under a general license contract may file a lawsuit if expressly authorized by the trademark registrant." Pursuant to the above provisions, an interested party in a registered trademark has the corresponding right to sue. The scope of interested parties includes licensees under a registered trademark license contract, and a licensee under an exclusive license contract may file a lawsuit with the People's Court. Sanhe Fucheng Company, as the licensee under an exclusive license contract for the registered trademark in question, is a proper plaintiff in this case.

II. Regarding the issue of whether the actions of the defendant Kunming Fucheng Company constituted proper use of its enterprise name within reasonable limits, or constituted infringement upon the registered trademark rights of another person.

First, pursuant to Article 99 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, a legal person enjoys the right to its name. In this case, the defendant Kunming Fucheng Company acquired its enterprise name right prior to the time the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company acquired the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801. Both the exclusive right to use a registered trademark and the enterprise name right are civil rights protected by law. Whether exercising the exclusive right to use a registered trademark or the enterprise name right, the right holder shall adhere to the principle of good faith and avoid causing a conflict of rights through improper exercise.

Second, pursuant to Article 14 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, establishing a branch is a lawful right of a legal person. It is not improper for Harbin Fucheng Company to register and establish the defendant Kunming Fucheng Company as its branch and to use the enterprise name in question in the name of that branch. The plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company's request for Kunming Fucheng Company to cease using the enterprise name containing the characters "福成" (Fucheng) lacks legal basis.

Third, pursuant to Paragraph 2 of Article 7 of the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Protection of Service Marks, the normal use by others of customary signs in the service industry, as well as the normal use of trade names (enterprise names), personal names, place names, and names of service premises to indicate the characteristics of the service or to explain matters relating to the service, shall not constitute an act of infringement upon the exclusive right to use a service mark. The operation mode of the catering industry generally involves storefront operations. Prominently using the enterprise name in conspicuous locations of the storefront (such as signboards and door headers) enables consumers to accurately and intuitively identify the service provider. Using the full enterprise name is less likely to reinforce consumers' impression of the enterprise name component. Therefore, in long-term commercial practice, a simplified use has gradually developed, retaining only the enterprise name component. However, a reasonably simplified use of an enterprise name should include both the enterprise name and the industry nature component to ensure the basic identifiability of the enterprise name, and it must not deliberately highlight the enterprise name component; otherwise, it would exceed the scope of proper use. The defendant Kunming Fucheng Company is an enterprise engaged in catering services. "肥牛" (fat beef) is a generic name for a raw material. The expressions used by Kunming Fucheng Company, such as "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot), and "福成肥牛火锅昆明旗舰店" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot Kunming Flagship Store), include the enterprise name and reflect the approved business scope of the enterprise, without highlighting the enterprise name component "福成" (Fucheng). This constitutes a reasonably simplified use of the enterprise name and does not constitute an infringement upon the lawful rights and interests of the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company.

In summary, the defendant Kunming Fucheng Company did not infringe the plaintiff Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use a registered trademark, and Sanhe Fucheng Company's claims could not be sustained. Accordingly, on November 24, 2006, the Kunming Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment: All claims of Sanhe Fucheng Company were dismissed. Case acceptance fee of RMB 5,510 was borne by Sanhe Fucheng Company.

Sanhe Fucheng Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yunnan High People's Court, requesting the reversal of the original judgment and a new judgment in its favor. The main reasons were: 1. Pursuant to Article 1(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademark Disputes, prominently using characters identical or similar to another person's registered trademark on identical or similar goods, where such use is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public, constitutes trademark infringement. The original judgment incorrectly imposed the prerequisite that the trademark registration time must precede the approval and registration time of the enterprise name component for the application of this provision, which lacks foundation. 2. Simplified use of an enterprise name must adhere to the principle of good faith and must be filed with the competent registration authority. Registered trademark No. 1344801 enjoys high market recognition. Harbin Fucheng Company was a customer of the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company before establishing Kunming Fucheng Company and was fully aware of the recognition of registered trademark No. 1344801, yet it maliciously used the trademark characters "福成" (Fucheng), without any filing procedure. Its use does not constitute a reasonable simplification of an enterprise name. 3. Sanhe Fucheng Company's "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot) constitutes a well-known service. The decoration, advertising language, and menu of Kunming Fucheng Company are identical to the unique name and unique decoration of Sanhe Fucheng Company, thereby constituting unfair competition. 4. The illegal business turnover of Kunming Fucheng Company can be determined according to law, and its operating profit should serve as the basis for damages. Additionally, Sanhe Fucheng Company presented new evidence proving that registered trademark No. 1344801 had been lawfully transferred back to Sanhe Fucheng Company by Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd., and that Sanhe Fucheng Company is the owner of the trademark right in this case. In summary, the original judgment had unclear factual findings and erroneous application of law, and should be reversed by a new judgment.

The respondent, Kunming Fucheng Company, argued: 1. Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd. was dissolved in March 2005, extinguishing its civil capacity and capacity for rights. The appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's acquisition of the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801 is therefore invalid, and Sanhe Fucheng Company has no right to bring this lawsuit as the owner of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. 2. Kunming Fucheng Company is a branch lawfully established by Harbin Fucheng Company in Kunming City and enjoys the enterprise name right according to law. 3. Kunming Fucheng Company's use of expressions such as "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot), and "福成肥牛火锅旗舰店" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot Flagship Store) constitutes a reasonably simplified use of its enterprise name and does not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of Sanhe Fucheng Company. The respondent requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

The following additional facts were found by the Yunnan High People's Court at the second instance:

On December 14, 1999, the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company obtained the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801. This trademark is a composite mark consisting of Chinese characters, pinyin, and a graphic (the upper part is the Chinese characters "福成"; the lower part is the pinyin "fucheng" accompanied by an ox-head pattern). The designated services are restaurants, hotels, and animal breeding. On May 21, 2003, Sanhe Fucheng Company transferred this trademark to a third party, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd. On August 18, 2004, Hebei Sanhe Fucheng Cattle Raising Co., Ltd. entered into a *Trademark License Contract* with Sanhe Fucheng Company and issued a *Power of Attorney*, clarifying that Sanhe Fucheng Company obtained the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801 and the right to independently initiate litigation for rights protection. On November 17, 2006, Sanhe Fucheng Company reacquired the trademark and became the owner of the exclusive right to use registered trademark No. 1344801.

"福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot) is a well-known hotpot service continuously operated by the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company for many years. This service has received recognition from relevant authorities and the market, has formed a certain market scale, and has developed dozens of franchise stores in multiple provinces and cities across the country. The signboards of these franchise stores all fully display registered trademark No. 1344801 and texts such as "福成肥牛" (Fucheng Fat Beef), "福成" (Fucheng), "福成肥牛城" (Fucheng Fat Beef City), and "福成肥牛海鲜城" (Fucheng Fat Beef Seafood City).

The respondent Kunming Fucheng Company is a branch lawfully established by Harbin Fucheng Company. Harbin Fucheng Company was established on June 10, 1999, and Kunming Fucheng Company was established on August 19, 2005. Both Harbin Fucheng Company and Kunming Fucheng Company had long-term business dealings with the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company and had repeatedly purchased Sanhe Fucheng Company's "福成" (Fucheng) brand beef from it.

The respondent Kunming Fucheng Company operates a hotpot catering business at its registered location in Kunming City. On the signboards, exterior walls, interior and exterior decorations, promotional materials, ordering cards, menus, and other items at its business premises, it prominently displays texts such as "福成" (Fucheng), "福成集团" (Fucheng Group), "福成肥牛" (Fucheng Fat Beef), "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅昆明旗舰店" (Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot Kunming Flagship Store); it hangs a beef cut diagram inside the store and creates menus matching the names of beef cuts indicated on the diagram (such as "眼肉" [Ribeye], "外脊" [Striploin], "上脑" [Chuck roll], "S眼肉" [S Ribeye]); it uses the advertising slogan "吃福成肥牛福到事成" (Eat Fucheng Fat Beef, Fortune Arrives and Success Comes) on in-store promotional banners; on signboards and light boxes, it displays a pattern of a cartoon cow holding a flag accompanied by the characters "福成" (Fucheng). Additionally, on outdoor light boxes, it displays the text "龙福成肥牛火锅" (Long Fucheng Fat Beef Hotpot), where the character "龙" (Long) is noticeably smaller than the characters "福成" (Fucheng).

Since its establishment in 2005, the respondent Kunming Fucheng Company has paid a total of RMB 557,324 in business tax, with a total turnover of RMB 11,146,480.

The disputed issues at second instance were: 1. Whether the respondent Kunming Fucheng Company infringed the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use a registered trademark; 2. Whether the actions of Kunming Fucheng Company constituted unfair competition; 3. If the actions of Kunming Fucheng Company constituted infringement, the amount of damages to be determined.

The Yunnan High People's Court held at second instance:

I. Regarding the issue of whether the respondent Kunming Fucheng Company infringed the appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

In this case, the written portion of Trademark Registration No. 1344801, to which the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company holds the exclusive right to use the registered trademark, comprises the Chinese characters "福成" (Fucheng). The Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company uses the characters "福成" as its trade name in its business premises. The exclusive right to use the registered trademark of Sanhe Fucheng Company and the right to the enterprise name of Kunming Fucheng Company are both rights established in accordance with law. The law, on one hand, protects the exercise of rights in accordance with law, and on the other hand, prohibits the abuse of rights. With respect to the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, Article 44 of the Trademark Law stipulates: "Where a registered trademark is used in any of the following manners, the Trademark Office shall order the registrant to rectify the situation within a specified period or shall cancel the registered trademark: (1) where the registered trademark is altered without authorization; (2) where the name, address or other registered particulars of the registrant of the registered trademark are altered without authorization; (3) where the registered trademark is assigned without authorization; (4) where the use of the registered trademark has ceased for three consecutive years." Article 51 stipulates: "The exclusive right to use a registered trademark is limited to the trademark that has been approved for registration and to the goods on which its use has been approved." According to the above provisions, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is limited to the trademark that has been approved for registration and the goods on which its use has been approved. The law protects the complete use of a registered trademark and prohibits the altered use or partial use of a registered trademark through unauthorized changes. In this case, Sanhe Fucheng Company used its Registered Trademark No. 1344801 completely and prominently on the signboard of its business premises, which constitutes lawful use. In contrast, whether Kunming Fucheng Company's use of its enterprise name constitutes lawful and normal use is the key issue in this case. Article 1(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Trademarks provides: "Using words identical or similar to another person's registered trademark as the trade name of an enterprise on identical or similar goods in a prominent manner, which could easily cause the relevant public to be confused, constitutes an act that infringes upon another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark." Therefore, to determine whether Kunming Fucheng Company infringed upon Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark, it is necessary to examine whether Kunming Fucheng Company's use of its name was normal use and whether such use could easily cause confusion among the relevant public.

1. Whether the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company's use of its enterprise name was normal use.

Article 39 of the Implementation Measures for the Registration and Administration of Enterprise Names, issued by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, stipulates that an enterprise shall use its name in good faith. Article 20 of the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration, issued by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, clearly stipulates: "The name used on an enterprise's seal, bank account, signboard, and letterhead shall be identical to the enterprise name registered. For enterprises engaged in commerce, public catering, services, and other industries, the enterprise name on the signboard may be appropriately simplified, but such simplified name shall be filed with the registration authority for record." Article 2 of the Reply of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Issues Concerning the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (Gongshangqi Zi [2001] No. 28) clearly stipulates: "The names of enterprise branches shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration." According to the above provisions, enterprise names should generally be used in a standardized manner, and when used, they should be identical to the registered enterprise name. Specific industries are permitted to appropriately simplify the use of enterprise names in accordance with the principle of good faith and as permitted by law, but such simplification is limited to use on signboards. The enterprise name registered by the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company is "Harbin Fucheng Catering Co., Ltd., Kunming Branch." However, it did not use its enterprise name in a standardized and complete manner on its business premises. On the contrary, Kunming Fucheng Company extensively used characters such as "福成" (Fucheng), "福成集团" (Fucheng Group), "福成肥牛" (Fucheng Fatty Beef), "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot), and "福成肥牛火锅昆明旗舰店" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot Kunming Flagship Store) on its signboards, exterior walls, interior and exterior decorations, promotional materials, reservation cards, and menus, which are inconsistent with its registered enterprise name. The law only grants an enterprise the right to "simplify" its enterprise name in accordance with law, but does not grant an enterprise the right to arbitrarily change its enterprise name. Simplification is a reasonable reduction based on the full name, rather than a complete abandonment of the original name and arbitrary use of a new name entirely different from the original name. Moreover, the law stipulates that the simplification of an enterprise name is only permitted for use on signboards and must be filed with the registration authority for record. Kunming Fucheng Company's conduct clearly violates the law; therefore, Kunming Fucheng Company did not use its enterprise name normally.

2. Whether the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company's use of the characters "福成" (Fucheng) could easily cause confusion among the relevant public.

From the specific circumstances of the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company's use of the characters "福成" (Fucheng), Kunming Fucheng Company had an intention of unfair competition in violation of the principle of good faith and subjectively had the intent to cause confusion as to the source of services. First, above the signboard of Kunming Fucheng Company's business premises, there was a light box for the registered trademark "龙福成" (Long Fucheng), to which Kunming Fucheng Company claimed it held the trademark right. The trademark itself is a cartoon cow holding a flag accompanied by the characters "龙福成" (Long Fucheng). However, the light box displayed the cartoon cow holding a flag accompanied by the characters "福成" (Fucheng). Kunming Fucheng Company intentionally altered the characters of its trademark, making them identical to the characters of Sanhe Fucheng Company's registered trademark. Second, the exterior light box of Kunming Fucheng Company's store bore the characters "龙福成肥牛火锅" (Long Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot), where the character "龙" (Long) was noticeably smaller than the other characters, objectively highlighting the characters "福成" (Fucheng). Third, considering Kunming Fucheng Company's other specific uses of the characters "福成" (Fucheng), such as the extensive use of characters inconsistent with its enterprise name—"福成集团" (Fucheng Group), "福成肥牛" (Fucheng Fatty Beef), "福成火锅" (Fucheng Hotpot), "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot), and "福成肥牛火锅昆明旗舰店" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot Kunming Flagship Store)—on reservation cards and business premises decorations, Kunming Fucheng Company was strengthening the impression of the two characters "福成" (Fucheng) in consumers' perception by highlighting them, diluting the origin of the characters "福成" (Fucheng), and making it unclear to the public whether "福成" (Fucheng) is part of Sanhe Fucheng Company's trademark or part of Kunming Fucheng Company's enterprise name. Furthermore, considering the objective fact that both Harbin Fucheng Company and Kunming Fucheng Company had long-term business dealings with Sanhe Fucheng Company and were aware of the relevant circumstances of Sanhe Fucheng Company's registered trademark in dispute, it can be determined that Kunming Fucheng Company had an intention of unfair competition and improperly used its enterprise name in violation of the principle of good faith. Article 7, Paragraph 2 of the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Protection of Service Marks, issued by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, provides: "The normal use by others of customary signs in the service industry, and the use in a normal manner of trade names (shop names), names, place names, names of service premises, to indicate service characteristics, or to explain service matters, does not constitute infringement of the exclusive right to use a service mark, except where there is a clear intention of unfair competition." Since Kunming Fucheng Company did not use its trade name normally and had a clear intention of unfair competition, the application of this provision in the original judgment to determine that Kunming Fucheng Company did not infringe Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use the registered trademark constituted an error in the application of law.

Second, from the perspective of the consequences of the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company's improper use of the characters "福成" (Fucheng), which form part of the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's disputed registered trademark, it would objectively cause ordinary consumers to have confusion and misunderstanding regarding the subject of the right. First, from a visual impression perspective, the disputed registered trademark is a combined trademark consisting of the Chinese characters "福成" (Fucheng) and the Pinyin "fucheng" combined with a bull's head pattern. The Chinese characters "福成" (Fucheng) are located in the upper part, which typically has a stronger visual appeal, and are the visually prominent part of the trademark. The Pinyin and the pattern are combined together and located in the lower part, which has weaker visual appeal and appears relatively blurred and not very prominent from a visual effect perspective. Generally, when consumers see this trademark, their visual attention is first drawn to the Chinese characters "福成" (Fucheng). After seeing the disputed registered trademark and Kunming Fucheng Company's enterprise trade name ("福成" (Fucheng)) on different occasions, consumers would form a perception of visual similarity. Second, from the perspective of understanding the Chinese character parts of the disputed trademark and enterprise name, an enterprise name can usually only achieve its identification function through the semantic expression of Chinese characters. In this case, the disputed enterprise trade name "福成" (Fucheng) is semantically identical to the visually prominent Chinese character part "福成" (Fucheng) of the disputed registered trademark, which is likely to cause consumers to perceive that the subjects are the same or have a close connection. Coupled with the fact that Kunming Fucheng Company did not use its enterprise name normally on its business premises, but instead prominently used the characters "福成" (Fucheng) on signboards, exterior walls, interior and exterior decorations, etc., it is easy for the relevant public to be confused or misled.

In summary, the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company used the characters "福成" (Fucheng), which are identical to the characters in the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's registered trademark, as the trade name of its enterprise and prominently used them on identical services, which could easily cause confusion among the relevant public. This conduct has constituted an infringement of Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use Registered Trademark No. 1344801.

II. Whether the conduct of the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company constituted unfair competition.

Article 5 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) stipulates: "An operator shall not adopt the following unfair means in market transactions to harm competitors: (1) counterfeiting another person's registered trademark; (2) using, without authorization, the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known product, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to that of another person's well-known product, thereby causing confusion with that person's well-known product and leading purchasers to mistake it for that well-known product; ..." According to the above provisions, using, without authorization, the unique name, packaging, or decoration of a well-known product, or using a name, packaging, or decoration similar to that of another person's well-known product, thereby causing confusion with that person's well-known product and leading consumers to mistake it for that well-known product, constitutes an act of unfair competition. The Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company argues that the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company, by using, without authorization, the unique name "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot) of this well-known service and its decoration, constitutes unfair competition. Kunming Fucheng Company insists that it is using its own enterprise name and does not constitute unfair competition. "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot) is a well-known hotpot service operated by Sanhe Fucheng Company for many years. This case has the prerequisite for applying Article 5(2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Kunming Fucheng Company prominently marked "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot), the unique name of Sanhe Fucheng Company's well-known hotpot service, at its business premises. This conduct is likely to cause consumer confusion and has constituted unfair competition.

III. How to calculate the amount of compensation for infringement.

The Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company used the characters "福成" (Fucheng), which are identical to the characters in the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's registered trademark, as the trade name of its enterprise and prominently used them on identical services, and also used, without authorization, the unique name "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot) of Sanhe Fucheng Company's well-known hotpot service, causing consumer confusion. This conduct has constituted an infringement of Sanhe Fucheng Company's exclusive right to use Registered Trademark No. 1344801 and also constitutes unfair competition. Kunming Fucheng Company shall bear tort liability, cease the infringement, eliminate the adverse effects, offer an apology, and compensate for losses.

Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Trademark Law provides: "The amount of compensation for infringement of the exclusive right to use a trademark shall be the profits gained by the infringer during the period of infringement as a result of the infringement, or the losses suffered by the infringed party during the period of infringement as a result of the infringement, including the reasonable expenses incurred by the infringed party in stopping the infringement." Paragraph 2 provides: "Where the profits gained by the infringer as referred to in the preceding paragraph, or the losses suffered by the infringed party, are difficult to determine, the people's court may award compensation of not more than RMB 500,000 based on the circumstances of the infringement." Article 20, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "Where an operator violates the provisions of this Law and causes damage to the infringed operator, it shall bear the liability for damages. If the losses of the infringed operator are difficult to calculate, the amount of damages shall be the profits gained by the infringer during the period of infringement as a result of the infringement; and the infringer shall also bear the reasonable expenses paid by the infringed operator in investigating the infringer's unfair competition acts that infringe upon its lawful rights and interests." In this case, because the evidence adduced by the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company is insufficient to determine the profits gained by the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company from the infringement (operating profits) or the losses suffered by Sanhe Fucheng Company from the infringement, the amount of compensation in this case shall be determined in accordance with Article 56, Paragraph 2 of the Trademark Law, at an amount not exceeding RMB 500,000. Since its establishment in 2005, Kunming Fucheng Company has paid a total of RMB 557,324 in business tax, with a total turnover of RMB 11,146,480. The compensation amount of RMB 200,000 requested by Sanhe Fucheng Company is reasonable and shall be upheld.

Accordingly, the Yunnan High People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 5, 2007:

1.  The first-instance civil judgment rendered by the Kunming Intermediate People's Court of Yunnan Province is reversed;

2.  The Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company shall immediately cease the unlawful use of the characters "福成" (Fucheng) from the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company's Registered Trademark No. 1344801 and the unique name of its well-known service "福成肥牛火锅" (Fucheng Fatty Beef Hotpot);

3.  The Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, publish a statement in the *Kunming Daily* to apologize to the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company and eliminate the effects of the infringement;

4.  The Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, compensate the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 200,000;

5.  The other claims of the Appellant Sanhe Fucheng Company are rejected.

The case acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance are each RMB 5,510, all to be borne by the Appellee Kunming Fucheng Company.

This judgment is final.
